stem.en: Kabir says: "If mitochondria are bacteria, I could grow some in a dish without a cell." What has changed in two billion years?

text.en: Most of the mitochondrion's genes have moved to the host's nucleus. It cannot make most of its own proteins; the host makes them and ships them in. A mitochondrion outside a cell starves within hours. Partner became part.

feedback.en: They survive briefly and cannot divide, because the recipes for most of their parts are in the nucleus they left behind.

text.en: Mitochondria are not really bacteria any more, so the story is wrong.

feedback.en: Descended from bacteria and no longer free-living is exactly what the story predicts.
Inside the cell they are protected. Outside, the problem is that they lack most of their own recipes.

explanation.en: Two billion years of partnership moved the recipes. The mitochondrion is a bacterium that outsourced its genome to its landlord.
